contract.summary: The violation list, filtered and paged — the Home and Files views read it.

commands.description: One route, two response SHAPES: a bare array by default, and a `{violations, total}` envelope as soon as `limit` or `offset` is greater than zero. Rules disabled in `config.json` are filtered out first; results are sorted by severity, then newest first.

options.description: Query parameter. Which analysis to read. An id that resolves to nothing is not an error — the route serves its empty answer.
Query parameter. Keep only code violations in this file. Matched against both the absolute path and the value as given, so a repo-relative path works.

Query parameter. Which lifecycle states to include. `active` is `new` + `unchanged`. Anything outside the three values reads as `active`, silently — the parse is a two-branch ternary, not a validation.

Query parameter. Comma-separated severities to include. Values are trimmed and lower-cased, and any value outside the five is DROPPED rather than refused — a filter of only unknown values leaves an empty list, which is then treated as no filter at all (probe-verified: `?severity=bogus` returns the unfiltered set).
Query parameter. Page size. `parseInt` with an `|| 0` fallback, so a non-numeric value, a zero, and an absent parameter are all "no limit" — the whole filtered set comes back.

Query parameter. How many to skip. Same `parseInt || 0` parse. A non-zero offset alone (no limit) switches the response to the envelope shape but pages nothing — the slice only applies when a limit is set.
